detail: The 151.338 ns / 849-stage delay attributed to alu is almost entirely the div_restoring_32 32-step restoring divider, which is unconditionally instantiated and combinationally connected to the final ALU output mux, so it dominates the timing graph for every alu_control value, not just DIVU/REMU. The catalogue's own guidance says a deep combinational arithmetic block like this can only be closed by pipelining/retiming it into stages or by making it multi-cycle -- but every one of those requires inserting at least one register clocked by clk somewhere in the divide path. alu's current port list has no clk input at all (src_a, src_b, alu_control, alu_result, zero only), and the port-list-preservation rule forbids changing the target module's ports, so no register can legally be added inside alu, and div_restoring_32 cannot be given a clock either since alu has no clock to forward to it as a submodule. A multi-cycle/valid-ready fix would also require the parent (execution_stage) to learn to wait, but execution_stage is alu's parent, not a child instantiated by alu, so it cannot be included in submodules per the scoping rule -- only children of the target may be rewritten alongside it. That rules out pipeline and retime (retime also needs an existing register boundary inside alu, and there is none). logic_restructure cannot help either: the case-statement output mux is already a flat select, and the actual critical recurrence is the divider's own 32 sequential subtract-compare-shift steps, which are dependent on each other by construction -- reordering the surrounding mux/case logic does not shorten that recurrence, and we do not have div_restoring_32's internal source to restructure its stages, only its port interface. Rewriting it from scratch risks silently changing its structure or falling back to a behavioral '/' operator, which the rules explicitly forbid as it just reintroduces the same depth under a different name and turns the equivalence check into an unprovable arithmetic theorem. fsm_encode and duplicate_driver do not apply: there is no state machine here and the failure is logic depth, not fan-out. Given the target's interface cannot legally acquire a clock, and no depth-preserving restructuring can shorten an inherently serial 32-iteration divider whose internals are opaque to us, no catalogue transform can be honestly applied to this path without breaking either the port-list rule, the parent-scope rule, or the arithmetic-structure-preservation rule.

which_path: Path runs from processor_0/pipeline_id_ex's src_mux_sel_2_out latch, through processor_0/ex_stage (execution_stage instance) into the soc_obs[7] flop; 151.338ns of the 156.7589ns total (96.5%) is burned inside processor_0/ex_stage/alu_ex, specifically its instantiated div_restoring_32 unsigned divider used for DIVU/REMU.
why_evidence: 96.5% (151.338ns) of 156.7589ns and 849 combinational stages are attributed to alu_ex alone; div_restoring_32 is a 32-iteration radix-2 restoring divider whose iterations are serially dependent, and this same block is blamed on 15 distinct critical paths across 200 endpoints.
fix_rtl: logic_restructure: rebuild div_restoring_32 as a radix-4 restoring divider that resolves 2 quotient bits per iteration (parallel compare against 1x/2x/3x divisor) instead of 1, cutting the serially-dependent iteration count from 32 to 16. The algorithm stays a structural restoring divider (no '/' operator, no registers added/removed), so latency is unchanged but the dominant serial chain on this path is roughly halved.
fix_tool: none -- the divider has already been through resizing/buffering; its delay comes from 32 data-dependent serial subtract-compare-shift stages, not from weak drive or routing, so no cell swap or buffer insertion can shorten a serial dependency chain. Only restructuring the algorithm (or pipelining it, which would need a latency change across modules not visible here) can reduce it.
